picked.title: CONTRIBUTING.md staging command fails on deleted files
picked.body:
The "Safe staging" section ends with `git add -u -- src/counter.ts src/typescript.svg`. Those two files aren't in the repo anymore, so the command now fails with `fatal: pathspec 'src/counter.ts' did not match any files`.

**Where:** `CONTRIBUTING.md`, around line 59.

**Done when:**
- The broken line is removed (or fixed if you find a reason to keep it)
- Running the whole staging block on a fresh clone gives no errors

**Hint:** use `git log` on those two paths to see when they were removed.
picked.fitReason: Mentions .ts files and you write TypeScript.
picked.difficultyReason: It is a simple documentation fix involving the removal of non-existent file paths.

others.title: Add labels for screen readers to the upload inputs and buttons
others.body:
The UI has no `aria-*` attributes or `<label>` elements at all. The kernel and initramfs file pickers only have a styled `<div>` above them, so a screen reader announces them as just "file". The hex text box only has a placeholder. And the emoji icons inside buttons get read out loud ("television Noise").

**Where:** `src/main.ts`, the HTML template from about line 48 to line 186. The main spots are the hex textarea (~147), `kernel-input` (~159), `initrd-input` (~162), and the `btn-icon` spans in every button.

**Done when:**
- The textarea and the two visible file inputs each have a real label (`<label for>` or `aria-label`)
- The emoji spans are hidden from screen readers
- The page looks the same as before
- `npm run build` passes

**Hint:** turning the existing caption `<div>`s into `<label>`s gives you the labels without changing the layout. Check your work with your browser's accessibility inspector.
others.fitReason: Mentions .ts files and you write TypeScript.
others.difficultyReason: The issue provides specific line numbers, clear instructions, and a direct hint on how to implement the fix.

others.title: Use the log panel instead of alert() when no kernel is selected
others.body:
If you click "BOOT LINUX" without picking a kernel, the app shows a browser `alert()` popup. Every other error in the UI goes to the log panel with `addLog(...)`, so this one sticks out and blocks the page.

**Where:** `src/main.ts`, around line 776, inside the `btn-boot-linux` click handler.

**Done when:**
- No `alert()` calls are left in `src/main.ts`
- Clicking BOOT LINUX with no kernel shows a clear message in the log panel, styled like the other errors
- `npm run build` passes

**Hint:** look at how the hex upload handler a bit lower down reports "No hex input provided".

skipped.title: Add unit tests for the APK package-name helpers
skipped.body:
Two small functions that work out an app's package name have no direct tests:
- `descriptor_to_package` in `src/android/apk.rs` (around lines 93–101) turns `Lcom/foo/Bar;` into `com.foo`
- `parse_text_manifest` in `src/android/axml.rs` (around lines 36–53) reads our small text manifest (`package=...`, `activity=...`)

**Done when:**
- There are at least 3 tests for `descriptor_to_package`: a normal class, a class with no package (like `LFoo;`), and a string missing the `L` or `;`
- There are at least 3 tests for `parse_text_manifest`: package and activity both present, package only, and no `package=` line (which should return an error)
- `cargo test --lib` passes, and the count goes up by the number of tests you added

**Hint:** both functions are private, so put the tests in a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block at the bottom of the same file. `src/android/runtime.rs` has an example of that layout.

skipped.title: README says 116 tests, but there are 140 now
skipped.body:
The README still says we have 116 unit tests. Running `cargo test --lib` today gives 140 passing.

**Where:** `README.md`, line 5 (the "tests" badge, both the image URL and its alt text) and line 16 (the "What works today" list).

**Done when:**
- Both places show the number you get from `cargo test --lib`
- Your PR description pastes the last line of the test output

**Hint:** the number in the badge lives inside the shields.io URL, so change it there too.
